key_insight: GREx expands referring-expression tasks beyond single-target cases by introducing datasets and a unified approach that handle single-, multi-, and no-target expressions across segmentation, comprehension, and generation.
problem_solved: Existing REx benchmarks and models assume one expression maps to one object, ignoring multi-target and no-target scenarios; this limits real-world applicability and evaluation of RES/REC/REG systems.
method: Introduce three new benchmarks that annotate single-, multi-, and no-target referring expressions to enable generalized evaluation.

Use a unified vision–language framework with a shared encoder and task-specific heads for RES (segmentation masks), REC (detection/localization), and REG (expression generation), trained jointly to transfer knowledge across tasks.
Design loss functions and training strategies to handle multiple target instances and explicit no-target cases (e.g., multi-target-aware matching and negative/no-target supervision).
impact: GREx enables more realistic training and evaluation of referring-expression models, improving robustness for real-world applications (e.g., human–robot interaction, image search) and promoting cross-task transfer between segmentation, detection, and language generation.
visual_elements: Side-by-side examples: single-target, multi-target, and no-target images with ground-truth masks/boxes and expressions
High-level model diagram: shared vision-language encoder with three task-specific heads (RES/REC/REG)

paper_title: GREx: Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation, Comprehension, and Generation
paper_authors: Henghui Ding, Chang Liu, Shuting He, Xudong Jiang, Yu-Gang Jiang
